newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 11.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - June 11.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

Deputy Defence Minister Anuruddha Ratwatte says troops expected attack by separatist Tamil guerrillas on the army's "tail" as troops advanced in northern rebel-held territory. He says troops successfully repulsed pre-dawn attack on defences at Thandikulam.
Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) damage air force Mi-24 helicopter gunship which came to provide air cover to ground troops who were under attack at northern Thandikulam.

Leader of Democratic United National Lalith Front (DUNLF) Srimani Athulathmudali, who was sacked from cabinet by President Chandrika Kumaratunga on Monday, says her party will continue to support Kumaratunga's ruling People's Alliance in parliament.
At least 20 soldiers and 30 LTTE rebels killed in attack on Thandikulam early on Tuesday. Rebels destroy armoury, blow up bridge at Nochchimoddai and fire artillery at Vavuniya further south.
Sri Lanka has recorded more than 30,000 cases of child sexual abuse by local and foreign paedophiles over the past few years, Probation and Childcare Services Department says.
Government plans to continue its war against LTTE while striving to introduce a lasting peace through its devolution package, Justice Minister G.L. Peiris says.
